image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on blue water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a brown/grey chest and body, and a dark tail with curled feathers. The bill is yellow-green with a black tip. The reflection of the duck is visible in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat. The coloration is yellow-green with a dark tip, matching the description for a mallard drake.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is compact and sits low in the water, indicating buoyancy. The plumage appears dense and smooth, typical of waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the classic mallard pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brownish-grey body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are submerged underwater and not visible in this specific pose. Therefore, this checkpoint cannot be visually verified.
The folded wings are visible along the side of the body. While folded, they appear broad and taper towards the tail, consistent with the anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear of the duck. The central feathers show a slight upward curl, characteristic of drake feathers.
